title: The Schubert bialgebra
abstract: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $Ξ_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Schützenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.

title: Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains
abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.

title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $κ$ for which they are $κ$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.

title: Generating functions of hypermaps and m-constellations with two alternating boundaries
abstract: We study the enumeration of planar hypermaps with several alternating boundaries. We first derive a peeling recursion with an arbitrary number of alternating boundaries and, in the two- boundary case, translate it into a functional equation for the corresponding generating function. Our main result is an explicit solution of this equation for m-constellations. In particular, we obtain a rational expression for the genus-zero two-point function, or cylinder generating function, with two alternating boundaries.

title: Well-posedness of 2D stochastic parabolic-parabolic Keller-Segel system with logistic source
abstract: We consider a stochastic, fully parabolic Keller-Segel system with multiplicative noise in non-divergence form and a logistic source in a two-dimensional bounded domain, subject to random initial data. We construct a global-in-time, non-negative martingale solution by means of a suitable regularisation procedure, combined with Banach fixed-point arguments, a localisation procedure, and a stochastic compactness method. We further establish pathwise uniqueness and uniqueness in law for martingale solutions, and prove the existence of a unique global-in-time, non-negative weak solution without imposing any smallness condition on the initial data.

title: Strict monotonicity of weighted inhomogeneous percolation thresholds under covering maps
abstract: We study Bernoulli bond percolation under weak covering maps for a class of weighted inhomogeneous product measures such that each edge $e$ carries a positive weight $w(e)$ and is open at intensity $λ\geq 0$ with probability $1-\exp(-λw(e))$. We prove a strict monotonicity of the weighted critical intensities $λ_c$ in the covering compatibility setting under bounded degree, uniform ellipticity, tame fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. While for the weighted uniform connection thresholds $λ_{\mathrm{conn}}$, we establish their strict monotonicity for non-injective weak covering maps under bounded degree, covering compatibility, uniform ellipticity, bounded-fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. Moreover, we verify a general-profile theorem on strict monotonicities of the two thresholds $λ_c$ and $λ_{\mathrm{conn}}$ respectively under explicit compact-interval finite-energy, derivative bounds and aforementioned geometric conditions.

title: Decomposing URLLC Deadline Failures in Beam-Managed 6G Networks: Implications for Mission-Critical Wireless Systems
abstract: Mission-critical wireless systems require ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), which sixth-generation (6G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam-managed networks are designed to provide. However, the reported URLLC deadline miss rate often masks the specific causes of packet failures. This paper introduces a framework that categorizes missed URLLC packets into three causes: queueing-limited (Q), transmission-limited (T), and beam-tracking-limited (B). Our analysis across ten scenarios with antenna counts from $\mathbf{64}$ to $\mathbf{4096}$ reveals three key findings. First, the dominant cause of missed packets shifts from Q to B when the antenna count exceeds roughly $\mathbf{1825}$. Therefore, operators of hyper-massive arrays should focus on improving beam-tracking accuracy to reduce the miss rate. Second, the beam-sweep period ($T_{\mathrm{sw}}$) significantly affects B-misses, while Q and T remain relatively unchanged. Reducing $T_{\mathrm{sw}}$ from $\mathbf{20}$ms to $\mathbf{10}$ms can cut the B-misses by more than half, without requiring a redesign of the scheduler. Third, Q-misses reach a cumulative distribution function (CDF) of approximately $\mathbf{0.98}$ by $\mathbf{0.8}\,$ms, so modest latency-budget relaxation can accommodate most overruns. In contrast, B-misses remain unsaturated at $\mathbf{12}\,$ms, making them difficult to accommodate within practical application-layer latency limits. Overall, this framework transforms an ambiguous aggregate miss-rate metric into a clear three-way diagnostic tool that directly informs remedial actions for network operators.

title: Quadratic mixing for the Lee--Sidford Dikin walk
abstract: Let $K=\{x\in\R^d:Ax\ge b\}$ be a bounded full-dimensional polytope with $m$ inequalities. For targets on $K$ with density proportional to $\exp(-\vartheta^\transpose x)$, we prove a $\widetilde O(d^2)$ bound, measured in Markov chain iterations, for the chi-square mixing of the $1/2$-lazy Metropolis Dikin walk based on a polylogarithmically rescaled Lee--Sidford metric. The estimate holds for every initial law with finite chi-square divergence. The proof controls the reverse Gaussian proposal through a quantitative average self-concordance estimate at the required $O(1/d)$ scale. We establish this estimate from uniform analytic derivative bounds for the Lewis-weight subspace and an all-order projection-weighted contraction inequality for Gaussian chaoses. For order $j$, the latter bounds each base-point polynomial at scale $d^{j/2}$, up to $j$-dependent and logarithmic factors. Truncating at logarithmic order then absorbs the remaining pathwise loss. This resolves, in the affirmative, the open problem of whether the Gaussian Lee--Sidford Dikin walk mixes in $\widetilde O(d^2)$ iterations: the previously stated quadratic bounds \cite[Theorem~1.4]{LLV20}, \cite[Theorem~1.2]{GKM24} rest on reverse-proposal steps identified as unresolved in \cite[Section~1]{Kook26}, whose $\widetilde O(d^{9/4})$ bound was the best rigorously established rate prior to this work. The proof is found by ChatGPT 5.6 Pro.

title: Bounded Leaf Volumes and Analytic Quotients of Singular Holomorphic Foliations
abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation of dimension $k$ on a compact Kähler manifold $M$ of dimension $n$. Suppose that the volumes of its regular leaves are uniformly bounded, $\dim(Sing\mathcal{F})<k$, and the union of the leaf closures meeting $Sing\mathcal{F}$ has finite $2k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. We prove that the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space of dimension $n-k$. The quotient map is proper and holomorphic, with connected fibers. The proof uses Bishop's theorems, Remmert and Stein extension, Barlet's cycle space, and Stein factorization. Away from the images of separatrices, the quotient has local charts given by finite holonomy groups. Examples show that these images need not coincide with the singular set of the quotient, and that bounded leaf volumes alone do not imply Hausdorffness. In codimension one, Malgrange's theorem makes the separatrix measure assumption automatic when $codim(Sing\mathcal{F})\geq 3$.

title: Solving the Tikhonov Regularization of the Total Least Squares Problem by matrix simultaneous diagonalization via congruence
abstract:
We are concerned with solving the Tikhonov regularization of the total least squares (TRTLS)
  which minimizes a sum of a quadratic fractional function and a nonnegative penalty quadratic form.
  If the penalty is nonsingular, the problem is attained and has been solved efficiently. However,
  if the penalty is singular, the problem becomes much more complicated, it may not be attained.
  In this paper we explore the property of simultaneously diagonalizable via congruence
  of matrices to make a change of variables and transform the problem into one of three tractable formats. Each of which is then
  thorough analyzed.

title: UAV Rotatable Antenna under Rotation Delay
abstract: Rotatable antennas (RAs) can improve wireless link performance by adjusting their boresight directions. However, existing RA studies generally assume instantaneous antenna reconfiguration, whereas mechanical rotation incurs non-negligible delay in practical deployment. To address this issue, we develop a rotation-delay-aware communication model for finite communication slots, where mechanical rotation directly reduces the time available for data transmission. This model reveals a fundamental tradeoff between the communication gain achieved through RA reorientation and the associated transmission-time loss. Accordingly, we formulate a rotation-delay-aware joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming to maximize the minimum effective transmission rate. For the single-user system, under a sufficient condition for strict concavity, the global optimum falls into one of three regimes: no rotation, partial rotation, and full rotation. A closed-form approximation is derived using a second-order expansion. For the multi-user system, we separate rotation-budget selection from fixed-budget max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization. An analytic-gradient zero-forcing (AG-ZF) algorithm is then developed for low-complexity joint RA orientation and rotation-budget optimization. The results show that explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential for finite-slot RA-enabled UAV communications, and that the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain and transmission-time loss while achieving favorable effective-rate performance with low computational complexity.

title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We do it by proving a new sufficient condition for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, which perhaps can be used to derive stronger results of this kind in the future.

title: A Non-Split Motohashi Formula for Toric Periods over Number Fields
abstract: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.

title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it. The resulting quantum GEXIT function has area equal to the number of encoded qubits per channel use for any stabilizer code, and this applies to the depolarizing channel through its joint four-valued Pauli-error distribution. For CSS codes on the quantum erasure channel and under independent bit- and phase-flip noise, the logical correction problem separates into two binary coset-decoding problems. On the quantum erasure channel, the duality between the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it gives a folding identity at complementary erasure probabilities. Using this and the area theorem, we derive an upper bound on the rate of code families with vanishing logical error probability that matches the capacity of the quantum erasure channel. For the depolarizing channel, we also derive a rate-dependent converse, using a connection between correction-class entropy and coherent information to establish an inequality involving the complementary channel.

title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1
abstract: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(η, ν) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:Σ^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.

title: Transposed Poisson structures in graded and algebroid geometry
abstract: We ask whether the transposed Leibniz rule $2z\cdot[x,y]=[z\cdot x,y]+[x,z\cdot y]$ survives the two passages that turn Poisson algebras into geometry, the shift of degree which produces Gerstenhaber algebras and the passage from algebras to algebroids. We introduce graded transposed Poisson algebras with a bracket of arbitrary degree and show that the parity of the degree decides which shape the answer takes. In even degree, over a unital base, such brackets are in bijection with homogeneous derivations, and on the exterior algebra of a vector bundle in degree zero they are exactly the gauge derivations of the bundle. In odd degree the bracket is forced to be the product with a single element of that degree, so a non-negatively graded algebra carries no non-zero transposed Gerstenhaber bracket. In particular, for a Lie--Rinehart algebra $(A,L)$, the Schouten--Rinehart Gerstenhaber algebra $Λ_A L$ is transposed if and only if the anchor and the bracket of $L$ both vanish. We then introduce transposed $F$-algebroids and classify those with an identity: if the rank is at least two the anchor vanishes and the structure is the datum of a derivation of the multiplication, while if the rank is one the bundle is trivialised by the identity and the structure is, globally, the Jacobi bracket of a single vector field. For the tangent $F$-algebroid of an $F$-manifold $M$ this forces $\dim M=1$.

title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers
abstract: We study two questions about the second-order Zarankiewicz numbers. The first is the recursive-line equality $z_2(m,n)=z_{RL}(m,n)$, known to hold in every computed case and conjectured in general. The second, here called \emph{overtake}, is the strict inequality $z_{2A}(m,n)>z_2(m,n)$ between the second-order augmented number and the second-order number. Both are governed by the number $H_{\mathrm{limited}}(m,n)$ of unoccupied cells in a limited extremal configuration. We prove that the first increase $z_2\to z_2+1$ already costs three unoccupied cells, forcing a unit of one-edge deficit, and the cell identity then bounds the excess $z_{2A}-z_2$ by $\lfloor(H_{\mathrm{limited}}-1)/2\rfloor$. In particular, when the recursive-line hole count is at most two, no overtake occurs. We conjecture the sharp budget $\lfloor H_{\mathrm{limited}}/3\rfloor$ and that $H_{\mathrm{limited}}\ge5$ is the threshold for an overtake. In the computed range $n\le7$, no overtake occurs at any order, the sole exception being the known case $(4,4)$. The recursive-line equality $z_2=z_{RL}$ is verified at every order in the range where both values are determined; the orders at which it remains unsettled are $(12,4)$ and $(14,4)$ at width four, $(11,5)$ at width five, and $(8,7)$ at width seven.

title: Exact lattice resonances and a sharp second Picard obstruction for the two-dimensional inviscid primitive equations
abstract: We study periodic perturbations of a rest state with constant stable stratification for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without viscosity or thermal diffusion on a fixed rectangular torus. Fourier resonance analysis and Sobolev estimates show that, despite unitary linear evolution, the polarized second Picard operator admits no bilinear bound losing less than one derivative at any Sobolev order and any fixed nonzero time for real data with zero vertical means. The loss is sharp for \(s\ge2\), with matching bounds on every sufficiently high physical dyadic shell. We classify exact lattice resonances in all signed channels and compute their polarized coefficients. A mixed-branch family with fixed vertical frequencies isolates diagnostic transport and shows that finite vertical regularity cannot reduce the loss below one horizontal derivative in tensor-product Sobolev spaces. In contrast, for \(s\ge2\), the horizontal mean of the second Picard operator admits a time-uniform one-derivative bound. In interaction variables, the response divided by time converges to the resonant operator, with an \(O(|t|^{-1})\) error after a four-derivative loss for \(s\ge4\). Finally, among real linear spaces defined solely by a common Fourier-support constraint on both components, the maximal spaces on which the full nonlinearity vanishes for all smooth states are precisely those supported on primitive lattice rays. On these rays, we construct explicit global solutions and obtain an exact criterion for uniform strict stratification.

title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
abstract:
The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma.
  In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.

title: The Spectral Theory of Threshold Graphs: A Survey
abstract: Threshold graphs-the $\{P_4, C_4, 2K_2\}$-free graphs, equivalently those built from a single vertex by repeatedly adding isolated or dominating vertices-are among the most thoroughly studied graph classes in spectral graph theory. This survey collects results on the spectrum of threshold graphs across the full range of matrices studied in the literature: the adjacency, Laplacian, and signless Laplacian matrices; the distance, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian matrices; the eccentricity and Seidel matrices; and the normalized adjacency, Laplacian matrix-together with the associated graph energies, cospectrality questions, extremal spectral radius problems, and several generalizations (weighted, quasi-threshold, hypergraph, and random threshold graphs). We emphasize results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Chvátal--Hammer, Merris, Bapat, and Jacobs--Lazzarin--Trevisan--Tura. We also present a study of integral threshold graphs (those with all-integer spectrum) across all seven matrices. We close with a list of open problems and conjectures drawn directly from the surveyed literature and from this new analysis.

title: On Niu's Conjecture for Two-Station Tandem Queues
abstract: In this paper, we prove a long standing conjecture in queueing theory made by Niu (1980): in a two-station tandem queueing system with constant service time (c) at station 1, the stationary average waiting time at station 2 is nonincreasing in c. Two very different proofs are provided: one for the general case and one for a special case in which the arrival process is Poisson and the service time at station 2 is exponential.

title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
abstract: We prove that $(α(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $α$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].

title: Normal approximation for total magnetization in subcritical long-range Ising models
abstract:
We establish Berry--Esseen bounds and 1-Wassershtein bounds for the total spin of strictly subcritical zero-field Ising models with summable interactions. Let $J:\mathbb Z^d\to[0,\infty)$ be symmetric, satisfy $J(0)=0$, and $\|J\|_1:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^d}J(x)<\infty$. For a nonempty finite set $Λ\subset\mathbb Z^d$, consider zero-field Gibbs measure with free boundary conditions, in which a spin configuration $σ\in\{-1,+1\}^Λ$ has probability proportional to \[
  \exp\!\left\{
  β\sum_{x,y\inΛ}
  J(x-y)σ_xσ_y
  \right\}. \] Let $S_Λ:=\sum_{x\inΛ}σ_x$ be the total spin and $β_{\mathrm c}$ denote the critical inverse temperature. For every fixed $0\leqβ<β_{\mathrm c}$, we prove that \[
  d_{\mathrm K}\!\left(
  \frac{S_Λ}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S_Λ)}},G
  \right)
  \leq C_{β,J}|Λ|^{-1/2}, \] where $d_{\mathrm K}$ is the Kolmogorov distance, $G\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, and $C_{β,J}$ depends only on $β$ and $J$. For the fully periodized model on $(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, the corresponding rate is $L^{-d/2}$, uniformly in $L$. For the classical nearest-neighbor model, the Kolmogorov bound also holds for $-β_{\mathrm c}<β<β_{\mathrm c}$, covering both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions. We also obtain $1$-Wasserstein bounds with the same rates in the respective subcritical regimes. Both the Kolmogorov and $1$-Wasserstein bounds hold with the same rate under the corresponding infinite-volume free-boundary Gibbs measures.

title: KKM meets colorful Carathéodory
abstract:
The colorful Carathéodory theorem states that if $V_1,\dots,V_{d+1}\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;V_i$ for every $i$, then there exist points $v_i\in V_i$ such that $0\in\mathrm{conv}\;\{v_1,\dots,v_{d+1}\}$.
  We give a new proof based on triangulations and the classical KKM lemma. We lift the sets $V_i$ to parallel affine copies of $\mathbb R^d$ in $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ and use a triangulation of the resulting point configuration to construct a KKM cover. Using the same approach, we prove the very colorful Carathéodory theorem.

title: Separable elements and Bruhat orders
abstract:
We prove the curious fact that, in any Coxeter group, the intersection of a principal left weak order ideal $[e,x]_L$ with a principal right weak order ideal $[e,y]_R$ has a unique maximal element $\mathrm{lr}(x,y)$ under Bruhat order. We apply this to resolve a conjecture of Hart and Rowley on involutions in weak order ideals.
  This fact arises from, and is applied to, our study of the theory of separable elements in finite Weyl groups. We use it to prove that for $U=[e,u]_R$ in a Coxeter group $W$, the multiplication map $W/U\times U\rightarrow W$ is surjective, where $W/U$ is the Björner-Wachs generalized quotient. This resolves and generalizes a conjecture of the authors. For finite Weyl groups, we further prove that this map is bijective if and only if $u$ is separable, thereby classifying the splittings of finite Weyl groups into weak order intervals, and resolving the natural extension of a question of Björner-Wachs.

title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

title: Enumeration of small vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs
abstract: We find the 728 vertex-transitive directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(v,k,t,λ,μ)$ where $1 \le v \le 39$ and $k < v/2$ and $0 < t < k$. A table with parameters and automorphism groups and some additional data is given.

title: Compact Toeplitz Operators and the Geometry of Fixed-Radius Averages
abstract: We characterize compact Toeplitz operators with bounded complex-valued symbols on the Bergman space of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with $C^2$ boundary. For any fixed $R>0$, the operator $T_f$ is compact if and only if the Euclidean-volume averages of $f$ over Bergman geodesic balls of radius $R$ tend to zero at the boundary. This answers Zhu's fixed-radius question affirmatively on the unit ball. On the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$, $n\ge2$, averages over products of Bergman discs of fixed radii characterize compactness, whereas averages over genuine Bergman geodesic balls need not. For every sufficiently small fixed radius, we construct a bounded real-valued symbol, smooth in the domain, whose geodesic-ball averages tend to zero along every sequence approaching the boundary, while its Berezin transform converges to a positive value along one such sequence. Boundary scaling reduces the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space. We prove the required uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition expressed in terms of a Busemann height function.

title: Continuity of biaccessibility dimension for polynomials
abstract: For a polynomial $f$ of degree $d\geq 2$, its biaccessible set $B(f)$ consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function $f\mapsto {\rm dim}_H(B(f))$ is continuous on the entire space of degree-$d$ polynomials. Therefore $(\log d){\rm dim}_H (B(f))$ gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree $d$.

title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $ζ$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|^β$ on $I_θ := [ - (\log{T})^θ,(\log{T})^θ]$, for every $θ> 0$ and $β> 0$. As $β$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|ζ|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $σ$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $β_{c}(θ) := 2\sqrt{1 + θ}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $β\leq β_{c}(θ)$, and assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $β> β_{c}(θ)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.

title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
abstract: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$. By relating the bridgeless graph complex to the $K$-theory of graphs and the Quillen spectral sequence, we show that these classes remain linearly independent after pushforward along the extended Torelli morphism $\mathcal M_g^{ct}\to\mathcal A_g$. Finally, we prove that the realizations of the motivic Lie algebra arising from $\mathcal M_g$ and $\mathcal A_g$ have the same image in the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_g^{ct}$.

title: Exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings
abstract: We prove a criterion for detecting exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings of closed contact manifolds. The criterion concerns symplectomorphisms induced by free contact circle actions on the boundary, and it is expressed purely in topological terms. As an application, we show that one-point blow-ups of an infinite family of Brieskorn varieties admit exotic compactly supported symplectomorphisms.

title: An Adjoint Criterion for Left-Invariant $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields on Even-Dimensional Lie Groups
abstract: For a fixed positive real constant $m$, a real Lie algebra of even dimension $2k$ admits a nonzero left-invariant $m$-modified conformal vector field for some nondegenerate metric if and only if an adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. In that case, a solution exists with neutral signature $(k,k)$ and zero conformal factor. As an application, we classify the admissible four-dimensional Lie algebras and metric signatures; the only Lorentzian exceptions among the admissible algebras are $\mathfrak{aff}(\mathbb{C})$ and the diamond algebra. On a pseudo-Riemannian manifold of arbitrary indefinite signature, a nonzero $m$-modified conformal vector field forces lightlike geodesic incompleteness, even when its conformal factor is variable.

title: Density Bounds in Hua's Theorem for Prime Squares
abstract: We prove a density version of Hua's theorem in the five-variable case: if $\mathcal P$ is a subset of the primes with relative lower density greater than $0.82$, then every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is a sum of five squares of primes from $\mathcal P$.

title: Universal operators: topology and consequences of ISP failure
abstract: Assuming a negative answer to the invariant subspace problem for separable complex Hilbert spaces, we prove that every universal operator has a continuum of minimal infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces with pairwise trivial intersections. These subspaces can be chosen so that the restrictions are invertible and their powers decay at any prescribed geometric rate. For an affine composition operator on the Hardy space \(H^2(\D)\), we derive restrictions on the zeros, inner factors and Hardy regularity of generators, and construct minimal models with radial vanishing of any prescribed finite order. Independently of the invariant subspace problem, we identify the norm interior, closure and boundary of the universal operator class. Its interior is the Caradus--Pozzi class, its closure is the complement of the upper semi-Fredholm class, and its boundary consists of the operators that are neither upper nor lower semi-Fredholm.

title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
abstract: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence. We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties. We show that the extended Fourier-Mukai transform for bounded complexes of mixed Hodge modules has cohomology sheaves that are flat over the twistor line of $λ$-connections. This also gives an extension of Fourier transform of mixed Hodge modules to a compactification of the de Rham moduli space.

title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
abstract: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-Hölder continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2π|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-Hölder curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.

title: A holomorphic motion with non-subharmonic Hausdorff dimension
abstract: We present an example of a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set $λ\mapsto A_λ$ for which neither the Hausdorff dimension $\dimH(A_λ)$ nor the lower Minkowski dimension $\dimMl(A_λ)$ is a subharmonic function of~$λ$. This answers negatively a question of Fuhrer--Ransford--Younsi, and distinguishes these dimensions from packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly.

title: Geometric rigidity principles for $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures
abstract: We study generalized Young measures generated by $\mathscr{A}$-free measures, $\mathscr{A}$ a constant-rank operator, in a compactification of the value space adapted to an energy. Given an $\mathscr{A}$-quasiconvex integrand $G$ of linear growth with coercive recession function $G^\infty$, the unit sphere at infinity is replaced by the indicatrix $\mathbb{S}_G=\{G^\infty=1\}$, which need be neither convex nor symmetric. The two compactifications are equivalent, but in the adapted one the equality cases of the Jensen inequalities characterizing $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures become statements of convex geometry about $\mathbb{S}_G$. We prove the characterization in this setting, with a new streamlined proof of the inhomogenization step based on a dyadic martingale argument. We then show that if $\mathscr{A}$-free measures $μ_j\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}μ$ and their $G$-energies converge, then at $|μ^s|$-almost every point the concentration-angle measure is supported on the smallest exposed face of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$ containing the $G$-polar of $μ^s$; in particular, it never charges the set where $G^\infty$ differs from its convex envelope, which, by the automatic convexity of Kirchheim and Kristensen, does not meet the wave cone. The concentration on the singular part of $μ$ is elementary for every such sequence if and only if each point of the wave cone on $\mathbb{S}_G$ is an extreme point of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$, as for the Euclidean norm underlying Reshetnyak's continuity theorem; on flat faces of $\mathbb{S}_G$, rigidity degrades from a point to a face. Finally, we prove a transfer principle for the convergence of energies of $\mathrm{BV}$ maps under Dirichlet boundary conditions.

title: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of all planar graphs
abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no such colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a planar graph on $25$ vertices that needs four colours. Further, we give critical planar graphs on $25$ vertices with $52$ and with $51$ edges, an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

title: Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_μ$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $μ$ on $(0,1]$.

title: Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials
abstract: On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.

title: A new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds
abstract: We give a new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds, following the work of Balogh-Krisátly. Our proof extends also to equality cases of the strong Brunn-Minkowski inequality, introduced by Magnabosco-Portinale-Rossi.

title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.

title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
abstract:
We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2πc/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\).
  This answers unconditionally and quantitatively a question studied by Gonek and Sahay under the Riemann hypothesis and the pair correlation conjecture. In particular, at the time of their work, it was not known unconditionally that even two consecutive moderate gaps occur infinitely often for any fixed \(c>0\). The proof combines Lamzouri's Hilbert-space formulation of the Montgomery--Taylor second-moment method with local spectral estimates for simple critical-line zeros and a cluster-counting argument that accounts for multiple zeros and zeros off the critical line.

title: Integral Volume Criteria for Semilinear and Quasilinear Liouville Theorems on Complete Manifolds
abstract: Let $M$ be a connected complete noncompact Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $V_o(R)$ denote its ball volume. We prove Liouville theorems without any curvature assumption. For $p>1$ and $q>p-1$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{pq/(p-1)-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)/(p-1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative Sobolev weak supersolution of $-Δ_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. For $q>\max\{1,p-1\}$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{p-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative global distributional energy supersolution of $u_t-Δ_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. Consequently, the corresponding Cauchy problem has no global solution in this class with a nonzero nonnegative local $L^1$ initial trace.

title: The fractional Hénon-Lane-Emden conjecture and some critical nonexistence phenomena
abstract: We refine the proof method for the Hénon-Lane-Emden system and extend it to fractional orders $0<s<1$, proving subcritical nonexistence of positive classical solutions. And we find examples with $0<s<1/2$ and fixed nonzero weights for which existence and nonexistence occur at different points of the same critical hyperbola.

title: Single-Letterization of Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Static Time-Invariant Control (STIC) Systems
abstract: In settings such as online recommendation platforms, medical decision-making with interim summaries, and stochastic control with static plants, the underlying system is often static so that the next state depends only on the most recent action. Moreover, the true system state is high-dimensional and cannot be observed directly, so actions must be selected based on information received through a rate-limited communication link, which constrains the control performance. This leads to a fundamental rate-cost tradeoff$\unicode{x2014}$the minimum communication rate required to achieve a prescribed average control cost. We study this tradeoff for a class of static systems we term static time-invariant control (STIC) systems, namely, control systems in which the next state depends on the history only through the most recent control action via a time-invariant kernel. For general control systems$\unicode{x2014}$not necessarily static or time-invariant$\unicode{x2014}$our prior work characterized this tradeoff through the limit of a sequence of directed-information minimization problems. However, the dimension of these problems grows with the time horizon, making the limiting formulation computationally intractable. In the present paper, we show for STIC systems that this growing-size formulation admits a single-letter characterization. This identifies STIC systems as the control-side counterpart of Noisy Output is the STate (NOST) channels$\unicode{x2014}$one of the few channel models whose feedback capacity admits a single-letter characterization. This yields, to our knowledge, the first constant-size convex characterization of the rate$\unicode{x2013}$cost tradeoff beyond linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control.

title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors
abstract: Orthogonal arrays are foundational objects in combinatorial design theory and experimental design theory, with broad applications in computer science, coding theory, and cryptography. In this paper, we investigate the existence for mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors, and propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $Σ$-resolvable transversal designs. As a result, we show that the necessary conditions for the existence of such mixed orthogonal arrays are also sufficient, except for a small number of known exceptions and nine unsettled cases.

title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansion of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose mondromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddle points. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package Resurgence.jl

title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
abstract: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words. This gives a new proof that they form a boolean poset.

title: Cross-ratios and first order ordinary differential equations
abstract: We investigate the usefulness of the cross-ratio in the study of first order odes of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K,\;n\geqslant1$, where $K$ is a differential field of characteristic zero with algebraically closed field of constants. We discover along the way many differential algebraic identity between solutions to that equation. We also explain why the cross-ratio of any four solutions to such an equation is in general not constant when $n\geq3$ by exhibiting an obstruction which prevents its constancy when $n\geq3$. Finally to any separable polynomial $P_\varphi(z)=z^{n+1}+\varphi_1z^n+\varphi_2z^{n-1}+\ldots+\varphi_{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, over a differential field of meromorphic function on some domain of $\mathbb C$ with the usual derivation we associate a uniquely defined first order ode of the form $y^\prime=P_ny^n+P_{n-1}y^{n-1}+\ldots+P_1y+P_0,\;\; (P_i)_{0\leqslant i\leqslant n}\in K$ such that every root of $P_\varphi(z)$ is a solution to the said differential equation.

title: A Spectral Approach to Fixed Points in Product Spaces
abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix $A$. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and $r(A)\leq1$, then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--Göhde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.

title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
abstract:
Consider the bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $γ= n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Marčenko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $γ$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values.
  Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

title: Distributed Optimization over Simplicial Complexes via Topological Dirac Synchronization
abstract: We introduce a distributed optimization framework for systems with higher-order interactions represented by simplicial and cell complexes. Specializing global topological Dirac synchronization to gradient flows of strongly convex local objectives, we show that the synchronized equilibrium coincides with the minimizer of the aggregate cost, without Lagrange multipliers, dual variables, or saddle-point dynamics. Orientation-equivariant convex terms and cell-dependent dimensional targets allow the optimal state to be nonzero, as determined by joint per-dimension optimality conditions. Our algorithm couples signals across dimensions through the Dirac operator: nodes interact with edges, edges with nodes and faces, and faces with edges, enabling information exchange beyond graph-Laplacian methods. In the isotropic case, a Master Stability Function analysis yields a necessary and sufficient condition for local exponential stability: the product of the directional coupling strengths must be below the squared ratio of the strong convexity parameter to the spectral radius of the complex. A weighted Lyapunov argument accounting for non-normal Dirac coupling establishes global exponential convergence at the same rate. Finally, we identify a topological admissibility condition ensuring invariance of the synchronization manifold and coherent convergence of cells to the optimum, with no counterpart in classical graph-based distributed optimization.

title: Proof Perplexity: A Probabilistic Approach to Measuring non-triviality in Machine Generated Proofs
abstract: In this article, we propose a benchmark to quantify the non-triviality and novelty of machine-generated mathematical proofs compared to existing literature. Our core methodology uses a probabilistic measure to evaluate the non-triviality of the underlying mathematical arguments in comparison to the current \texttt{MATHLIB} library. Finally, we apply this benchmark to the recent proof generated by Claude on the complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function to test for non-trivial steps.

title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2
abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

title: The transition between order to disorder in the Seppäläinen-Johansson model
abstract: We study the Seppäläinen-Johansson model of first-passage percolation along a region of the plane where it moves from an ordered to a disordered phase, represented by a 2nd order discontinuity in its limit shape function. The fluctuations in this transition region are of order one, and we determine that certain limiting statistics are described by Fredholm determinants and are closely related to the largest eigenvalue of the GUE.

title: Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic
abstract: For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finitely presented group $G_p$ and elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ such that $ab=1$, $ac=0$, and $c\ne0$. Thus $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$, and the group algebra over every field of characteristic $p$, fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of $c$, so the proof does not require torsion-freeness.

title: Threshold and Below-Threshold Dynamics for the Energy-Critical NLS: The Higher-Kinetic-Energy Regime
abstract: We study the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation below and at the ground-state energy, focusing on solutions in the upper energy cone, characterized by \[ E(u)\le E(W),\qquad \|\nabla u\|_{L_x^2}>\|\nabla W\|_{L_x^2}, \] where \(W\) is the ground state. Unlike the lower cone, where compactness of critical solutions plays a central role in understanding the dynamics, such compactness is generally unavailable on the upper branch. Consequently, previous results have often required additional assumptions, such as finite mass or finite variance. In this paper, we remove the finite-mass assumption in the radial setting and give a complete characterization of the upper-cone dynamics in the natural energy space \(\dot H^1_{\mathrm{rad}}\), resolving an open problem posed by Duyckaerts and Merle\cite{DM08}. In particular, this establishes finite-time blow-up of the special threshold solution \(W^+\) in the negative time direction in dimensions \(d=3,4\). For non-radial data in dimensions \(d\ge5\), we show that {for solutions in the interior of the upper cone, the limit superior of their $\dot H^1$-norm satisfies an explicit lower bound as time approaches each endpoint of the maximal lifespan,} while forward-global solutions on the upper threshold sheet that remain below this level must coincide with \(W^+\) modulo symmetries. We also obtain a complete classification of upper-threshold dynamics for finite-variance data in all dimensions \(d\ge3\).

title: GPU-Accelerated Robust MA--RIS Pre-Optimization for Communication and Target Illumination
abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer strong spatial control for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), but repeatedly adapting MA positions and RIS phases to each channel realization can be impractical. This letter develops a GPU-accelerated robust pre-optimization framework that jointly selects slow-timescale MA geometry and RIS phases and returns a reusable Pareto set balancing expected worst-user rate and transmit-side worst-target illumination. The illumination objective measures directional transmitted power rather than complete echo-detection or parameter-estimation performance. The proposed Regime-Aware Multiobjective Pre-optimization (RAMP) preserves regime-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross-regime mating using Pareto-survival feedback, and constructs a worst-regime robust archive. Numerical results demonstrate competitive robust Pareto quality against the considered evolutionary baselines while avoiding online physical re-optimization.

title: General Relativity in Three Lines
abstract:
We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Plücker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Plebański action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint.
  A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.

title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.

title: Gaussian Identification in MIMO Channels
abstract: We study the identification capacity of discrete-time Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels under per-antenna, per-symbol peak-amplitude constraints. We establish upper and lower bounds on the identification capacity that scale linearly with the channel rank $r.$ The number of reliably identifiable messages can grow super-exponentially with blocklength $n,$ following $M_n(R)=2^{(n\log n)R},$ where $R$ is an achievable rate. The channel rank provides a spatial-multiplexing advantage, enabling higher achievable rates and, consequently, stronger super-exponential codebook growth. These results characterize the rank-dependent gain in achievable identification performance.

title: Sharp Bounds for Common Spanning Forests under Color Refinement
abstract: We study the common spanning structure of connected finite simple graphs that are indistinguishable by uniformly initialized color refinement. We prove that any two such graphs with common cyclomatic number $r\ge2$ contain isomorphic spanning forests with at most $r-1$ components. This bound depends only on $r$ and is sharp for every $r\ge2$. We also determine the maximum, over all such graph pairs without restricting their order, of the minimum edge symmetric difference under vertex bijections: it is exactly $4(r-1)$.

title: Triangle-free Rank--Ramsey graphs from ordered incidence lifts
abstract:
For a graph $G$ with adjacency matrix $A_G$ and a coefficient field $\mathbb K$, put $ρ_{\mathbb K}(G)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}(A_G+I)$. We answer the triangle-free Rank--Ramsey existence question of Beniamini, Linial and Shraibman. For every order $n$, we construct a triangle-free graph $H_n$ such that, simultaneously over all coefficient fields, $$
  ρ_{\mathbb K}(H_n)=\bigl(4(2/3)^{3/4}+o(1)\bigr)n^{3/4}, $$ with an error uniform in the field. The graphs can be chosen Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $n$. Our method combines ordered layers of point--line incidence flags with a common low-dimensional endpoint space. We determine the exact real rank, independence number and chromatic number of the affine lifts. For all triangle-free complete incidence lifts, we obtain a sharp two-term lower bound for complete incidence lifts, with sharpness witnessed by projective-plane incidence graphs over suitable coefficient fields. We also establish a third-order estimate and stability near equality. On the same explicit graphs, both the Lovász number and minimum semidefinite rank exceed the prescribed Boolean-matrix rank by polynomial factors. Thus neither parameter has a universal constant-factor upper bound in terms of complement rank. We determine Shannon capacity in the short-layer range.

title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
abstract: We propose two families of multigrid preconditioners for unfitted finite element discretisations of the Riesz maps of the de Rham complex, in H(grad), H(curl) and H(div), stabilised by cell aggregation. The first is a geometric multigrid method applied directly to the unfitted operators, on a hierarchy of background meshes that share the same boundary representation. Its smoothers are star patches built on the aggregated mesh, so that each patch captures the kernel of the stabilisation. The second is a multilevel auxiliary-space preconditioner that combines a patch smoother localised around the cut cells with the body-fitted problem on the active mesh, which is in turn solved by a non-nested geometric multigrid method. Both are used as building blocks of block-diagonal preconditioners for the mixed Hodge Laplacians. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on geometries with a controlled cut fraction and on general geometries, show iteration counts that are robust with respect to the cut configuration, the mesh size and the number of levels. We also report results for higher-order discretisations, weakly imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions and a face-based stabilisation.

title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
abstract: It has been conjectured that $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct. We first construct caterpillars $T_3$ and $T_4$ satisfying $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_3)=\ell(T_3)+3$ and $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T_4)=\ell(T_4)+4$, respectively. We then construct, for every positive integer $r$, infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic caterpillars with exactly $r$ internal vertices for which every bijective edge labeling is antimagic. Each such caterpillar $T$ satisfies $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)=|V(T)|=\ell(T)+r$. Consequently, $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)-\ell(T)$ is unbounded even within the class of caterpillars, and no absolute constant $C$ can satisfy $χ_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+C$ for every tree $T$.

title: The Involution Rank of $\MCG(Σ_3)$ Is Four
abstract: For the closed orientable surface $Σ_3$, we prove \[ \irank\MCG(Σ_3)=4.\] Thus $\MCG(Σ_3)$ can be generated by four involutions, but not by three. This settles the genus-three case of Farb's problem on generation by involutions.

title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
abstract:
Let $(A_{ij}(x))_{1 \leq i \leq N, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ be a matrix of univariate semialgebraic functions. We study the solvability of the system of linear inequalities \begin{equation*}
  \sum_{j=1}^M A_{ij}(x)F_j(x)\leq f_i(x) \ \ \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, N, \end{equation*} where we assume each forcing $f_i$ is a Nash function. We show that the $C^m$ solvability of the system can be characterized by finitely many linear ordinary differential inequalities in $f$ with semialgebraic coefficients depending only on $(A_{ij})$. When the system is solvable, the solution may be chosen semialgebraic, and the proof gives a constructive procedure in the semialgebraic sense. We also study the semimodule structure of admissible forcings, establishing finite generation and lack thereof in various settings.

title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
abstract: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial. The module $V$ is a quotient of the permutation module on the affine hyperplanes of an elementary abelian $p$-group, arising as a quotient of the absolute Galois group of $F$. We also describe $R$-trivial classes as sums of corestrictions of cup products involving a Kummer class.

title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
abstract: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-Güneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve. For the first two families we also give cyclic models over the projective line and relate the formulas to Elkin's rank formula. We then treat two classes of Artin-Schreier fibre products. A supersingular genus-six family has a-number $3$ at the zero parameter and $2$ elsewhere, although the genera and $a$-numbers of its quadratic quotients remain fixed. We determine its Ekedahl--Oort types as $(0,0,0,1,2,3)$ and $(0,1,1,2,3,4)$,

title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
abstract: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.

title: Probabilistic Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
abstract: We give applications of the probabilistic Fourier extension theorem for the paraboloid in d dimensions (see [Saw7] for the sphere, and the proof there holds for a smooth compact piece of the paraboloid) to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation with initial data f, in which we obtain sharp averaged Sobolev regularity results over certain `martingale transforms' of the intial data f. The deterministic analogue in three dimensions has been obtained recently by OpenAI [Ope].

title: Axis-parallel square packing with an exact formula for optimal packing of seven squares
abstract: How large a square is needed to hold axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths? We give exact formulas for the optimal side through seven squares, with explicit constructions and geometric lower-bound proofs. For every $n\ge6$, the optimum for $n$ squares is a sum of at most $n-3$ of the prescribed side lengths. This bound is sharp on an open set of side lengths and yields the optimal Euclidean Lipschitz constant $\sqrt{n-3}$ of the optimum as a function of the $n$ side lengths.

title: Complete regular dessins: the nonmetacyclic case
abstract: We classify regular dessins on $K_{2^e,2^f}$ with nonmetacyclic colour-preserving automorphism group, retaining the two specified vertex rotations. We give nonredundant presentations and exact counts in both the abelian and nonabelian Frattini cases. For orientation- and colour-preserving isomorphisms, the number is $2^{2e-2}+16$ when $e=f\ge4$ and $3\cdot2^{2f-3}+16$ when $e>f\ge4$, with explicit counts for all smaller exponents. The construction uses a parity criterion in the abelian case and a uniquely determined odd quadratic root with two lifts in the nonabelian case. A dessin in the classification is reflexible exactly when its Frattini subgroup is abelian. All symmetric classes are circular. We determine every circular subfamily, including its face orders and genera; the circular count is $2^e+8$ on the diagonal and $2^{f-2}(2^{f-1}+1)+8$ off the diagonal for $e\ge f\ge4$.

title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.

title: On strongly coherent confidence envelopes for the false discoveries
abstract: Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.

title: Computing Fréchet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fréchet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fréchet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya Inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.

title: Aligning Information Theory and Formal Verification: A Lean Formalization of Rate-Distortion Theory
abstract:
Large language models have recently demonstrated an ability to generate substantial mathematical proofs and formalizations, including machine-checked arguments for major open problems and classical theorems. These developments highlight a growing workflow in which AI systems search for proofs while proof assistants certify their correctness. Within information theory, however, formalized libraries remain limited, and existing formalized theorems focus almost exclusively on Shannon's foundational lossless theorems.
  This paper presents the first Lean formalization of core components of rate-distortion theory, a central framework for lossy compression and modern machine-learning analysis. We identify the alignment challenges that arise when translating information-theoretic definitions, such as distortion measures, typicality and achievability, into a proof-assistant setting, and we develop a reusable library of definitions and lemmas faithful to textbook conventions. Our formalization provides a foundation for future AI-assisted proofs in information theory and enables subsequent mechanized developments to build on a coherent, verified infrastructure rather than generating long proofs from scratch.

title: Eventual Exactness and Rigidity for Abelian Covers of Groups
abstract: For a group $G$, let $a(G)$ denote the minimum number of abelian subgroups covering $G$, and let $ω(G)$ be the maximum size of a pairwise noncommuting set. We prove the exact formula $\sup_{ω(G)\leq n}a(G)=2^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}+1$ for every $n\geq 63$. Equality holds precisely for groups with derived subgroup of order two and binary symplectic central quotient of dimension $2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The proof combines centralizer descent with a structural separation of nonscalar alternating commutator maps.
