We prove that an unit vector $h\in L^{p}(μ, X)^*$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(L^{p}(μ, X)^*)$ if and only if $\frac{h(t)}{\|h(t)\|}$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(X^*)$ for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $h(t)\neq 0$, where $X$ is a Banach space such that $X^*$ is separable. As an application of this result, under the same hypothesis on $X$, we prove that a point $f\in L^p(μ, X)_{1}$ is a very smooth point if and only if $\frac{f(t)}{\|f(t)\|}\in S(X)$ is a very smooth point for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $f(t)\neq 0$. We give several examples to show that these results does not hold for $p=1$.

title: Reconnection in 2D Inertial Magnetohydrodynamics
abstract: We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,α}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. We finally show numerical examples of magnetic reconnection, validating known rigorous results and uncovering new cases.

title: Revisiting separators in string graphs, region intersection graphs, and induced-minor-free graphs
abstract:
String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced vertex separators of size $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m})$ and conjectured that this bound can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families. A key intermediate step in Lee's approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs. In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee's approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. These results have since found applications in a wide range of works.
  Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee's padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee's as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov's separator results, and many works relying on them.
  In this work, we prove that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced separators of size $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, and more generally obtain analogous $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$ bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works. Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time.
  Our proof uses a different approach from Lee's and does not rely on padded decompositions. Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs.
  We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib.

title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.

title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
abstract: Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_α$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[Δ_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.

title: LCM Splittings in GCD Domains
abstract: In a GCD ring $R$, every pair of elements $a,b\in R$ admits a greatest common divisor $\text{gcd}(a,b)$ and a least common multiple $\text{lcm}(a,b)$. Motivated by a question on Mathematics Stack Exchange by Ash Seifert~\cite{Sei22}, I introduce the notion of an lcm splitting $c,d\in R$ for $a,b$ satisfying $cd\sim\text{lcm}(a,b), c\mid a, d\mid b, \text{gcd}(c,d)\sim1$. I show that adequate Bézout domains always admit lcm splittings, give examples of Bézout domains in which some pair has no lcm splitting, and make further remarks on this seemingly new property.

title: Dg models for derived differential operators
abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

title: Robust Local Fréchet Regression: Nonasymptotic Theory and Minimax Optimality
abstract: We develop robust local Fréchet regression for heavy-tailed responses in a general metric space and propose a distance-based median-of-means estimator. We derive nonasymptotic pointwise high-probability bounds separately under local second-order smoothness and local $1$-Wasserstein Hölder continuity, and show that the corresponding optimized rates match the classical pointwise rates for nonparametric regression. We also establish matching pointwise minimax lower bounds over embedded Gaussian regression subclasses. Remarkably, our results do not require an entropy condition on the response space. Simulation studies with positive-definite matrix-valued responses, together with a real-data application involving Wasserstein-valued responses, illustrate the robustness--efficiency tradeoff and practical performance of the proposed estimator.

title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
abstract: Matomäki proved that if $α\in\R$ is irrational, then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $|α-a/p|\le p^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$ for a suitable integer $a$. In \cite{BaMo}, Baier and the author established analogues of this result for $\F_q(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. In this paper, we extend it to all real quadratic extensions of $\F_q(T)$.

title: Order relations for the near geometric and near spectral geometric curves
The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

title: Fourier dimension for exactly approximable matrices
abstract: We determine the Fourier dimension of exactly approximation set for all dimensions. More precisely, let $m,n\ge1$, $\boldsymbolθ\in\mathbb R^m$, and $ψ:\mathbb N\to \mathbb R^+$ be a non-increasing approximate function. Denote by $\textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)$ the set of $m\times n$ matrices which are inhomogeneously $ψ$-approximable with shift $\boldsymbolθ$, but not $cψ$-approximable for any fixed $0<c<1$. We prove that $$\dim_{\text{F}} \textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)=\frac{2n}{1+τ_ψ},\ \text{whenever }τ_ψ>\frac{n}{m},$$ where $τ_ψ$ is the lower order of $ψ$ at infinity.

title: On conservativity of multitype continuous-state branching processes
abstract: In [4], Grey gives a condition on the branching mechanism $ψ$ of a continuous- state branching process Z ensuring that the process is conservative. This condition is obtained from the expression of the solution of the differential equation satisfied by the Laplace exponent of Z. In higher dimensions, it is generally no longer possible to make this solution explicit and very few conditions ensuring the conservativity of the process are known. In this paper, we provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for conservativity. For dimension 2, when types cannot regenerate themselves, we give a necessary and sufficient condition and we invert the Lamperti representation of the multitype branching process.

title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.

title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
abstract:
The confinement theorem of [CM1] gives Euclidean volume growth for a proper minimal submanifold whose height over a plane is sublinear. Such volume growth places strong restrictions on the geometry. This leaves linear height as the natural borderline and raises the question of which, if any, linearly growing cones still force Euclidean growth.
  Here we determine this borderline sharply for proper holomorphic curves in $C^2$. There are two sharp thresholds for the aperture depending on the Kähler angle $θ$ of the two-plane $Π$: $\tan(θ/2)$ and $\cot(θ/2)$. No proper holomorphic curve exists below the first, every such curve is algebraic below the second, and superquadratic proper holomorphic disks exist above the second. These conclusions extend to holomorphic submanifolds of arbitrary dimension and codimension.
  For stationary integral varifolds there are again three regimes: sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, narrow cones of aperture $\varepsilon$ force polynomial growth with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and wide cones allow arbitrarily fast growth. The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.

title: Reverse Urysohn inequality for functions and functional Shephard problem
abstract: The results obtained in this paper provide a generalization of some geometric inequalities to the class of log-concave functions. They describe the relationships between the Quermassintegrals of functions and bodies, giving estimates for constants involved in functional Shephard-type problems.

title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichmüller theory"
abstract: We first correct $\boldsymbolμ_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbolμ_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.

authors: J. H. M. ten Thije Boonkkamp
title: A Mixed Elliptic--Hyperbolic Monge--Ampère Problem: Modeling and a Least-Squares Solver
abstract: We consider a transport problem motivated by freeform optical design of a parallel-to-far-field reflector. Classical formulations rely on either elliptic or hyperbolic Monge--Ampère equations, leading to globally convex/concave or saddle-shape reflector geometries, respectively. However, the design of smooth reflector arrays may require optical surfaces combining both types of curvature. To address this, we introduce a mixed elliptic--hyperbolic Monge--Ampère system obtained by partitioning the source domain into one elliptic and one hyperbolic subregion, and we develop a least-squares method for its numerical approximation. Numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to compute both isolated and periodic mixed-type transport solutions, yielding smooth reflector configurations.

title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
abstract: For the biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces, we construct a nonconforming finite element method that requires neither stabilization nor the Piola transform. The reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element relies solely on vertex values and scalar edge moments. The same local construction applies to every triangle of a piecewise planar surface. The bilinear form consists of elementwise Laplacian inner products and permits standard finite element assembly. By separating the planar vertex residual from the angle defect contribution, we establish weak discrete Miranda--Talenti-type estimates on both planar meshes and closed piecewise planar surfaces. These estimates guarantee uniform stability on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes. We prove the well-posedness of the method, first-order convergence in the energy norm, and second-order convergence in the broken $H^1$ and $L^2$ norms. Numerical tests on three surfaces show the predicted convergence rates and examine the discrete Miranda--Talenti constants and angle defect scaling.

title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the complex plane
abstract: This paper continues our previous work \cite{Miy6} on an extension of the Li--Mochizuki theorem concerning the existence and uniqueness of complete diagonal harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles over open Riemann surfaces. We consider the extended Hitchin equation associated with general subharmonic weight functions on the canonical bundle, not necessarily induced by holomorphic $r$-differentials. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for arbitrary subharmonic weight functions, without additional regularity assumptions on them. We also prove that, on the complex plane, such a complete solution exists whenever the weight function is not identically $-\infty$. Furthermore, if $(\varphi_ε)_{ε>0}$ is a family of smooth subharmonic weight functions decreasing to such a weight function $\varphi$ as $ε\searrow0$, the associated family of smooth complete solutions $(h_ε)_{ε>0}$ with $\det(h_ε)=1$ converges monotonically to the unique complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$ and satisfying $\det(h)=1$.

title: Universality of Annealed Complexity in the Spherical Pure $p$-Spin Model
abstract: In an influential work, Auffinger, Ben Arous, and Černý (2013) investigated the limiting annealed complexity in the spherical pure $p$-spin model associated to the Gaussian disorder. Their results, in particular, included an explicit expression for the total number of critical points of the Hamiltonian below any given energy level. In this paper, we consider the same anneal complexity associated to a disorder interpolating between an arbitrary random variable and its Gaussian counterpart. Assuming strict subgaussianity of the former, our result shows that the annealed complexity shares the same limit as in the Gaussian case.

title: Dissipative solutions for fibred Wasserstein gradient flows of Cahn-Hilliard-type energies
abstract: We study fourth-order evolution equations with a fibred Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, describing spatial transport of finitely many or a continuum of types. The driving Cahn-Hilliard-like energy combines a diagonal gradient contribution with nonlinear interactions between types. We prove subsequential convergence of the fibred Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme to solutions satisfying an energy-dissipation inequality. For general type distributions, the absence of compactness in the type variable is addressed through defect-based solution concepts. On $\mathbb R^d, d\le 3$, we construct dissipative solutions satisfying an additional entropy-dissipation inequality. On smooth bounded domains in any space dimension, a coercivity estimate for the metric slope allows us to construct energy-dissipating solutions without relying on flow interchange, thereby covering non-convex domains endowed with the intrinsic length distance. In both cases, a variational comparison of the piecewise constant and De Giorgi interpolants yields a common limiting energy and strong convergence of the difference to zero without requiring strong compactness. For finitely many types, the defects vanish and the construction yields weak solutions. We further establish weak-strong uniqueness of dissipative solutions in every space dimension and of energy-dissipating solutions in dimensions $d\le5$. Combined with the respective existence results, this yields strong convergence of the variational approximations whenever a sufficiently regular, strictly positive solution exists.

title: Identifiability from Moments in Independent Component Analysis Mixture Models
abstract: We study Independent Component Analysis (ICA) mixture models. These models consist of mixtures of ICA densities. An ICA density is associated with a random vector whose coordinates become mutually independent after an invertible linear transformation. ICA mixture models are nonparametric extensions of the celebrated family of Gaussian mixtures. We show that in many cases the ICA mixtures are identifiable from the collection of the observed moment tensors, that is, the mixing coefficients, linear transformations, and source moments of order up to $d$ can be identified from the moment tensors of order up to $d$ for generic parameters. We address the problem by studying the corresponding secant varieties and their algebraic properties such as dimensions and Gauss maps. In particular, for $n$-variate distributions, we establish that generically and up to the trivial scaling and permutation symmetries, when $d\geq 5$, the parameters can be recovered uniquely for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ mixture components. For $d=3,4$, we show identifiability up to a finite equivalence class for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ and $0.5 n^{d-2}/d!$ components respectively, where for $d=4$ the mixing coefficients need to be known a priori. The obtained bounds on the component numbers have the maximum possible orders in $n$, and for $d = 3$ and $d\geq 5$, they are also asymptotically sharp.

title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.

title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
abstract:
We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic.
  To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.

title: Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods
abstract: This paper is concerned with the conditional Hölder regularity of the temperature for the heat-conducting compressible Navier-Stokes system, where the pressure takes a complete form that includes the Stefan-radiation correction. Under minimal assumptions on the density and velocity, we prove that any weak solution automatically exhibits Hölder continuity in the temperature component. This constitutes the main result of the work and is achieved by an application of the De Giorgi method. As a consequence of this conditional regularity, we establish the global-in-time existence of a regular, unique solution to a simplified system for the compressible potential flow of a heat-conducting fluid, valid for arbitrarily large initial data.

title: Error analysis of a backward L2 method on graded meshes for linear and semilinear subdiffusion equations
abstract: Time-fractional linear and semilinear parabolic equations with a Caputo time derivative of order $α\in(0,1)$ are considered. Their solutions exhibit an initial singularity of type $t^σ$ for any fixed $σ\in (0,1) \cup (1,2)$. A backward L2-type discrete fractional-derivative operator of order $3-α$ is considered on nonuniform temporal meshes. Sufficient conditions for inverse monotonicity of this operator areestablished. Hence, sharp pointwise-in-time error bounds are obtained on graded temporal meshes with arbitrary degree of grading. The theoretical findings are illustrated by numerical experiments.

title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
abstract:
Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$
  C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.

title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
abstract: With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.

title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
abstract: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,σ,χ_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.

title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
abstract: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.

title: Cuspidal Class Number Formulae for Intermediate Modular Curves of Prime Level
abstract: Let $X$ be a modular curve lying between $X_{0}(p)$ and $X_{1}(p)$, where $p \ge 13$ is prime. The cuspidal group of $X$ is the subgroup of its Jacobian generated by the equivalence classes of differences of cusps. In this paper, we give explicit formulae for the order of the cuspidal group, and two subgroups of it defined over the rationals.

title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
abstract:
This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*}
  u_t-|Du|^γF(D^2u)=f
  \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ γ>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (λ, Λ)$-elliptic with $0<λ\leqΛ$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,α)>0 $ such that \[
  |γ|+\left(\fracΛλ-1\right) \leq \varepsilon
  \quad \Longrightarrow \quad
  u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+α,\frac{1+α}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (γ, \fracΛλ) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.

title: Sharp $L^6$ Fourier moments and (3,$δ$)-energy estimates for fractal measures on the truncated cone in $\R^3$
abstract:
For a $δ$-separated $(δ,d)$-Katz--Tao set $P$ on the truncated cone in $\R^3$, $1<d\le 2$, we prove the sharp energy bound
  \[
  \E_{3,δ}(P)\lesssim_{\varepsilon} δ^{-\varepsilon}
  \max\{δ^{-(3d+2)},δ^{-(5d-1)}\}.
  \]
  The proof applies the Fu--Ren incidence theorem to triples with a fixed sum. As a corollary we also deduce a sharp $L^6$ moment estimate for the Fourier transform of Frostman measures supported on the cone.

title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
abstract: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(τ,ε)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivière's equation, $α$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.

title: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes
abstract: We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code. The constructions are the result of a computer search executing a tabu search algorithm.

title: Cavity collapse and kinetic energy concentration in three-dimensional free-boundary Euler flow
abstract: We construct smooth axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations in bounded domains for which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at a finite time $T$. The velocity has a single-valued potential, and the construction applies without surface tension and with any fixed positive surface tension. Both boundary components remain embedded and disjoint before collapse, while the outer boundary converges smoothly. The terminal outer meridional domain may be any smooth bounded simply connected domain whose closure is separated from the rotation axis; the interior point generating the collapse circle and the positive concentrated energy may be prescribed independently. We prove a sharp collapse law with radius asymptotic to an explicit multiple of $(T-t)^{1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{-1/4}$, determine curvature blow-up asymptotics, and show that kinetic energy concentrates uniformly on the circle. For a canonical reflection symmetric family, we identify a common cylindrical spacetime limit and sharp velocity and pressure profiles. At every fixed spatial point in the region enclosed by the limiting outer boundary and away from the collapse circle, the velocity tends to zero while the pressure tends to positive infinity. For this family, we characterize the topology of the limiting material map and prove its optimal $1/2$-Hölder regularity and sharp $W^{1,p}$ threshold $1\le p<2$, with first derivatives in weak $L^2$ but not in $L^2$. These canonical solutions admit weak continuations that preserve mass and momentum and whose total energy drops at collapse by exactly the concentrated kinetic energy.

title: Sharp maximum estimates for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients
abstract: In this paper we obtain sharp exponents in the Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci maximum estimate for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients, originally conjectured by Pucci in 1966 \cite{Pucci}, together with corresponding sharp results under the more natural quantification of uniform ellipticity in more than two dimensions. The proofs combine a Hessian integral inequality obtained from boundary Morse inequalities with an obstacle argument. The estimates also hold on arbitrary open sets, of finite volume, without regularity assumptions on their boundaries.

title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
abstract:
We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $μ_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^α}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $ν_t$ and its linear evolution $μ_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $ν_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant.
  We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $μ_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t Δ} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.

title: Disproof of Wright's Problems 14 and 15 on lacunary maximal functions
abstract: We disprove the proposed weak endpoint bounds in James Wright's Problems 14 and 15 from the 2017 collection of harmonic-analysis problems. For every $d\ge1$, we exhibit a fixed compactly supported singular probability measure with Fourier decay of every order $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, for which the dyadic convolution maximal operator has infinite weak $L^1$ and infinite $H^1$ to weak $L^1$ operator norms. For every finite nonempty set of dyadic scales, both optimal weak constants equal the number of scales, with the Hardy constant measured in the specified atomic norm. Increasingly separated renewal digits provide uniform real-frequency Fourier decay while allowing the disjoint output regions needed for the positive and mean-zero tests. We first establish the fixed measure, then prove the two endpoint estimates using separate normalized tests. Finally we prove the two Fourier lemmas used in the construction.

title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.

title: Stability of Hyperplane Projections of the Regular Simplex and $L_p$-Projection Bodies of balls in $\ell_q^n(\mathbb{R})$
abstract: We prove stability estimates for extremal hyperplane projections of the regular simplex. We further generalize the analogous stability estimates for $\ell_q$-balls by the first named author and the monotonicity theorem for normalized ratios by Barthe and Naor to the $L_p$-setting. To this end, we derive closed formulas for the support functions of their $L_p$-projection bodies, complementing those obtained by the second named author. A key ingredient in our proofs is a stability refinement of the majorization inequality for Gaussian mixtures.

title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem
abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture asserts that every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices has a quasi-kernel of size at most $n/2$, whereas the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture asks for a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood has size at least $n/2$. Spiro proved that the former implies the latter. In this paper, we establish a weighted transfer theorem: if every nonnegative integer weighting of a source-free digraph $D$ admits a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood contains at least a $θ$-fraction of the total weight, then $D$ has a quasi-kernel of size at most $\lfloor(1-θ)α(D)+θμ\rfloor$ for $0<θ\le1/2$, where $μ$ is the maximum matching size between a maximum independent set and its complement. Using the independent blow-up construction of Spiro, we deduce that the universal small and large quasi-kernel assertions are equivalent for every such $θ$, with no loss in the parameter. In particular, the two conjectures are equivalent. As an application, we prove the half-order bound for source-free break digraphs.

title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.

title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.

title: On MRD constacyclic codes over inseparable field extensions
abstract: In this paper, we construct MRD constacyclic codes of length $p$ over an inseparable field extension $L/K$, where $K$ has characteristic $p$. In particular, these codes cannot be obtained from known constructions.

title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
abstract: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.

title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.

title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
abstract: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.

title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
abstract: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.

title: Line spreads of W(2n-1, q), q even
abstract: Let q be an even prime power and n \ge 2. We construct line spreads of the symplectic polar space W(2n-1,q) by replacing pairwise disjoint reguli in a Desarguesian line spread. The construction is based on partitions of the points of PG(n-1,q^2) into points of a nondegenerate Hermitian variety and Baer sublines meeting that variety in exactly one point. In the plane case, the partition is invariant under a cyclic group of order q^2-q+ 1.

title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
abstract: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

title: Random Sampling of Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes
abstract: We study the effect of random sampling on stochastic processes whose finite-dimensional distributions are Bohr almost periodic under time shifts. The sampling times are generated independently by a two-sided random walk with positive increments or by a two-sided subordinator. Under a non-degeneracy condition we show that the shifted finite-dimensional distributions of the sampled process converge to those of a strictly stationary process. Consequently, if the sampled process is itself almost periodic in distribution, then it must already be strictly stationary. We further prove an $L^2$-law of large numbers for sampled averages under covariance decay and a uniform second-moment bound, and identify its limit with the mean of the stationary limit process. Finally, for $m$-dependent, $L^2$-uniformly integrable almost periodic processes, we establish a central limit theorem for the centered sampled sums, whose asymptotic variance is given by the autocovariance series of the stationary limit.

title: Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy
abstract: With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude information networks (LAINs) must provide reliable communication, environmental sensing, and target identification to support efficient and safe airspace operation. Although integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) provides a foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing, identification must also be incorporated to meet airspace safety and regulatory requirements. This paper reviews integrated sensing, communications, and identification (ISCAI) for LAE. We first review low-altitude communication, sensing, and identification approaches and explain how representative applications motivate their integration. We then summarize low-altitude ISAC fundamentals, including system architectures, channel modeling, unified signal models, and performance metrics, followed by communication-centric and sensing-centric designs, resource allocation, and aircraft trajectory optimization. Building on these, we introduce ISCAI, focusing on a backscatter communication (BackCom)-based identification mechanism in which backscatter devices serve as electronic license plates for aircraft. We present system and signal models for integrated sensing and identification (ISAI) and ISCAI, together with multifunctional receiver designs and mutual integration gains. Finally, we discuss open problems and future directions, including an information-theoretic framework, artificial intelligence-empowered system design, and reconfigurable intelligent surface-enhanced ISCAI. This review provides a structured perspective on the evolution of LAINs toward integrated communication, sensing, and identification.

title: Faber--Krahn inequality for homogeneous normalized $p$-Laplacian type operators
abstract: We establish a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the normalized (or game-theoretic) $p$-Laplacian, proving that, for $p\geq 2$, the ball uniquely minimizes the principal Dirichlet eigenvalue among bounded connected Lipschitz domains of prescribed volume satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition. More generally, we prove the same inequality for the family of homogeneous operators $|Du|^γΔ_p^N u$, with $p>1$ and $-1<γ\le p-2$. Unlike the classical $p$-Laplacian, these operators lack a variational structure, preventing the use of standard symmetrization arguments. Our proof overcomes this difficulty through a level-set approach: it relies on a flux identity for the eigenvalue, for which a variational interpretation re-emerges in the special case where the domain is a ball.

title: Locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras
abstract: For an Artin algebra $Λ$, we define the class of locally Gorenstein modules, which is a generalization of semi-Gorenstein projective modules and, therefore, a generalization of projective Gorenstein modules. For a locally Gorenstein module $X\in{\rm mod}\ Λ$ we construct $\underline{χ}_X$ a subcategory of $\underline{\rm mod}$ $Λ$ and we prove that the syzygy functor is faithful and full on $\underline{χ}_X$. Using that, we prove that the Igusa-Todorov functions $φ$ and $ψ$ vanish on the family of locally Gorenstein modules. Finally, using locally Gorenstein modules, we define the locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras, and we prove that their finitistic, and the $φ$ and $ψ$ dimensions are finite.

title: Lifting mod $p^n$ Galois representations
abstract: We generalize the results of Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis, which lift odd mod $p$ Galois representations to geometric $p$-adic representations, to geometric lifting theorems for mod $p^n$ representations whose mod $p$ reduction is odd.

title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
abstract: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. The proof is topological, using vanishing cycles and the theory of Lefschetz pencils. As an application, combined with a construction due to Miranda, we prove that for any positive rational number $δ$ there exist a blow up $Y \to X$ at finitely many points, an ample line bundle $M$ on $Y$ and a point $x \in Y$ such that $\varepsilon(Y,M,x) = δ$; Miranda proved this when $X = \mathbb{P}^2$.

title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.

title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
abstract: We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.

title: Are Single-Leader-Multi-Follower Problems Particular Cases of Bilevel Optimization?
abstract: For more than 20 years, single-leader multi-follower (SLMF) problems have been treated as a more difficult class of problems in comparison to bilevel optimization. In this work we challenge this common belief, studying whether SLMF problems can be reformulated as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. We consider both optimistic and pessimistic formulations. For the optimistic case the answer is positive: We derive an equivalent bilevel problem by representing the followers' equilibria as fixed points of the solution mapping of a single optimization problem. For pessimistic problems, the situation is different. We show that every optimistic trilevel problem admits an equivalent pessimistic SLMF formulation with two followers. Conversely, for every pessimistic SLMF problem verifying a mild attainability assumption we establish an equivalent optimistic trilevel reformulation. The reformulations are easy, readily tractable, and they preserve convex and linear data. Thus, unless $\text{NP}=Σ_2^p$, we deduce as byproduct that multiple followers induce an unexpected complexity gap between optimistic and pessimistic approaches, which is not the case when considering one follower alone.

title: Brennan's Conjecture and the Universal Integral Means Spectrum
abstract: In October 2026, OpenAI released two preprints \cite{openai-brennan,openai-kraetzer}, establishing Brennan's celebrated conjecture~\cite{brennan,brennan2} and disproving Kraetzer's more general $t^2/4$ conjecture \cite{kraetzer, kraetzer-thesis}. While validating these results, we observed that much of their argument is redundant and arrived at a drastically shorter proof of a significantly stronger statement. The goal of this note is to give a short and concise presentation of the reborn proof, sacrificing some of the context and consequences for brevity, and relegating them to a follow-up work. In this particular case the human-AI interaction was fruitful and quite satisfactory, and hoping for a similar future in other subjects, we would paraphrase Rick Blaine: {\em ``AI, we hope this is the beginning of a beautiful friendship.''}

title: Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Ampère Equations
abstract: We prove a Harnack inequality on Monge--Ampère gradient graphs under suitable geometric bounds, giving us interior $L^\infty$ estimates for the linearized Monge--Ampère equation. The proof combines Moser iteration on extrensic balls with a gradient estimate for the extrinsic distance function. The argument avoids the Caffarelli--Gutiérrez Harnack inequality and the engulfing and covering properties of Monge--Ampère sections.

title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture
abstract: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(χ(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4χ(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
